chunk_text: ### Search Enhancement Search engines use knowledge graphs to show structured information panels alongside traditional search results. When a user searches for a well-known person, organization, or place, the search engine can display structured facts (birth date, nationality, notable works) drawn directly from the knowledge graph. ## Key Challenges ### Incompleteness Most real-world knowledge graphs are incomplete — many true facts are missing. Freebase was estimated to be missing over 70% of birth places and 75% of nationalities for people in its database. Link prediction and knowledge base completion are active research areas addressing this. ### Noise and Inconsistency Automated extraction introduces errors. The same entity may appear under multiple names (coreference), and contradictory facts can coexist in a large graph built from diverse sources. ### Temporal Dynamics Real-world facts change over time. A person changes jobs, companies merge, and political boundaries shift. Temporal knowledge graphs add validity time intervals to edges to track when facts were true, but maintaining temporal consistency at scale remains challenging.

chunk_text: ## Training Methodology ### Pre-training LLMs are first pre-trained on a large unlabeled text corpus using a self-supervised objective. The most common objective is next-token prediction (autoregressive language modeling): given the preceding tokens in a sequence, predict the next token. The model learns to minimize the cross-entropy loss between its predicted probability distribution and the actual next token. BERT and its variants use a masked language modeling objective instead, where random tokens in the input are masked and the model must predict the original tokens using bidirectional context.

chunk_text: ### LanceDB LanceDB is an open-source, serverless vector database built on the Lance columnar format. It runs in-process (embedded) with no server required, supports SQL-like queries alongside vector search, and is designed for multimodal data (text, images, video). Microsoft GraphRAG uses LanceDB as its default local vector store. ### Zvec Zvec is an open-source, in-process hybrid vector database released in February 2026 (v0.5.0, June 2026). It is designed specifically for hybrid search — combining dense vector search with BM25 full-text search and scalar filtering in a single query call. Zvec uses Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) and weighted fusion to combine dense and sparse retrieval signals. Unlike FAISS or LanceDB, Zvec includes a built-in reranker, eliminating the need for a separate reranking model. Its in-process, serverless design makes it suitable for local AI applications and research prototypes where cloud dependencies are undesirable.

Common choices include FAISS (from Facebook AI Research), Pinecone, Weaviate, Chroma, and LanceDB. The choice of vector store significantly affects retrieval latency and memory usage.

chunk_text: # Vector Databases ## Overview A vector database is a specialized data store designed to store, index, and query high-dimensional vector embeddings efficiently. Vector databases are a core infrastructure component in modern AI applications, particularly in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, semantic search engines, and recommendation systems. Unlike traditional relational databases that index structured scalar values, vector databases are optimized for approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search — finding the vectors most similar to a query vector according to a distance metric such as cosine similarity, dot product, or Euclidean distance.

chunk_text: ## Core Concepts ### Embeddings An embedding is a dense, fixed-length vector (typically 384 to 4096 dimensions) that represents the semantic content of an input. Embeddings are generated by passing text (or images, audio, etc.) through a trained encoder model. The embedding model maps inputs to vectors such that semantically similar inputs produce nearby vectors. ### Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search Exact nearest neighbor search requires comparing a query vector against every stored vector — linear time complexity that becomes prohibitive at billion-vector scale. Approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) algorithms trade a small amount of recall for dramatically faster search. HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) is the most widely adopted ANN algorithm. It builds a multi-layer graph where each layer is a navigable small-world network. Queries start at the top layer and greedily descend to the bottom layer, following edges to progressively closer nodes. HNSW achieves sub-millisecond query times on million-scale datasets. IVF (Inverted File Index) partitions the vector space into clusters (Voronoi cells). At query time, only the nearest clusters are searched rather than the full dataset. IVF is memory-efficient and used extensively in FAISS.

chunk_text: ### LanceDB LanceDB is an open-source, serverless vector database built on the Lance columnar format. It runs in-process (embedded) with no server required, supports SQL-like queries alongside vector search, and is designed for multimodal data (text, images, video). Microsoft GraphRAG uses LanceDB as its default local vector store. ### Zvec Zvec is an open-source, in-process hybrid vector database released in February 2026 (v0.5.0, June 2026). It is designed specifically for hybrid search — combining dense vector search with BM25 full-text search and scalar filtering in a single query call. Zvec uses Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) and weighted fusion to combine dense and sparse retrieval signals. Unlike FAISS or LanceDB, Zvec includes a built-in reranker, eliminating the need for a separate reranking model. Its in-process, serverless design makes it suitable for local AI applications and research prototypes where cloud dependencies are undesirable.
